subject: Model v2.4 Deprecation Exception & Cross-Functional Comms
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Model v2.4 deprecation - exception request for Atlas Health / next steps

Team,

Quick context: we published the deprecation notice for model v2.4 last week (planned EOL 2026-06-01). Atlas Health (attached procurement thread) is asking for a 60-day extension on v2.4 because they have a validation pipeline tied to a tokenizer quirk that v3.x changes. They are a strategic healthcare customer (DEAL-4509) and procurement asked for an exception.

Asks:
- Dev (Dev) — can we support a short-term extension (60 days) to keep v2.4 running on hosted Dedicated for them without breaking other rollout timelines? If there are mitigations (quantization profiles/backport) state effort and risks.
- Product (Hannah) — need a comms plan and a customer-facing exception template. Also flag any quality/regression testing we should mandate before extension.
- Legal/Procure (Laura) — any billing/contract language we need for a 60-day exception? Is an amendment enough?
- Markus/Leadership — flag any SLA or risk objections.

Attachment: model-v2.4-deprecation-notice.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
Attachment: customer-exception-template.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

I can run the customer sync if we have alignment by EOD tomorrow (05/06).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0172

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model v2.4 deprecation - exception request for Atlas Health / next steps

Marissa, team —

Short answer: feasible, with caveats.

Notes from infra:
- We can keep v2.4 running specifically for Atlas Health by pinning their Dedicated pool to the v2.4 artifact and disabling automated model swap on that pool. That requires a minor routing exception and a config flag change (INF-2934).
- Effort: ~2 engineer-days to implement the routing guard, plus 1 day to add monitoring and an automated sunset job to ensure the instance terminates after 60 days.
- Risks: increased maintenance surface (security/patching still applies), and we will not be able to apply some v3 performance improvements to that pool. Also need a rollback playbook in case of latent bugs.

Technical asks:
- Access: I need the Atlas Dedicated cluster id and owner email to scope the change.
- Testing: recommend we require a smoke-test script from Atlas that validates tokenization and a short latency/throughput run. We should hold extension until that passes.

If leadership approves, I can schedule the work for Wed/Thu (05/06-05/07).

— Dev

Thanks Marissa and Dev —

Comms/PM perspective:
- We should grant a time-bound exception only after: (a) technical verification (Dev), (b) signed amendment that clarifies no new feature guarantees, and (c) updated evals passed for regression checks.
- I’ll draft a customer-facing note that explains: why v2.4 is deprecated, what the extension covers, explicit sunset date, and recommended migration checklist. I’ll use the customer-exception-template.docx and return a version by EOD 05/06.
- Internal comms: prepare a Jira ticket (INF-2934) and update the model catalog with the exception flag and a visible sunset date. Also add a known-issues entry in the release notes.

Questions for leadership:
- Do we want to centralize all exceptions (single canonical list) or let regions approve separately? For now I suggest central approval so we can track precedent.

I’ll coordinate the customer-facing sync after we confirm the technical and legal steps.

— Hannah

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the heads up. Atlas can provide the smoke-test scripts — we run those nightly already. A couple of asks from our side:
- If possible, we'd prefer a 90-day extension to finish the regulatory validation window. 60 days is tight for our compliance team.
- We need confirmation there will be no forced migration during the extension window and that tokens/ids remain stable.

We can sign an amendment; send over a template. If you can confirm timelines by EOD tomorrow, I’ll escalate internally.

Best,
Sarah Lim

Atlas Health

Marissa/Hannah —

Legal/procurement notes:
- Amendment is fine for a 60-day extension, but for 90 days we should route through Sales Ops and update the SOW. A 90-day ask triggers finance approval because it affects renewal timing (DEAL-4509).
- Suggested clause: "Customer is granted a one-time, time-bound exception to continue using Model v2.4 for the period starting [start_date] through [sunset_date]. Redwood will not introduce forced migrations to the customer's pinned environment during the exception period." We’ll add standard indemnities/limitations.
- Please include the cluster id and exact resources in the amendment to avoid ambiguity.

I’ll draft an amendment template and attach it to the HubSpot deal. Expect a first pass by 05/06 EOD.

— Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Model v2.4 deprecation - exception request for Atlas Health / next steps

Team / Sarah —

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Consolidated plan (agreed owners):
- Approval: Leadership (Markus) grants one-time exception for 60 days; Atlas to confirm acceptance of 60 vs 90.
- Engineering (Dev) to implement routing guard and smoke-test integration on 05/06–05/07 (INF-2934). Deliverable: routing change + automated sunset + rollback playbook.
- Product (Hannah) to produce customer-facing exception letter and migration checklist by EOD 05/06.
- Legal/Procure (Laura) to draft amendment and attach to HubSpot (DEAL-4509) by EOD 05/06.
- Sales (Marissa) will schedule customer sync for 05/08 (I’ll send invite once we have amendment draft).

Decision note for the record: Markus approved the 60-day exception to avoid setting a broad precedent for 90-day extensions. Any future extension requests will go to a central exceptions list.

Sarah — can you confirm acceptance of the 60-day window by Monday 05/10? If Atlas still needs 90 days we’ll route for finance review but we need that request in writing.

Attachments referenced: model-v2.4-deprecation-notice.pdf, customer-exception-template.docx
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2934, https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/4509

Appreciate the fast turn — will follow up with calendar invite.
